passage: My name is Pankaj, and last term I said yes to five tutoring batches because the money looked good. By the second week I was teaching until nine at night, then trying to do my own assignments. I missed two morning lectures. I fell asleep during a lab. My friend Shankar lent me his notes and asked, kindly, if I was okay. I said the money was worth it. Then the internal test results came out and my marks had dropped in three subjects. The extra income for the month had been real. But so was the cost, and I only saw it when the sheet arrived. I had been counting money and forgetting everything else.

qa.q: How many tutoring batches did Pankaj take?
What did Pankaj feel when the test results came out?
qa.a: Pankaj felt dismayed at the drop in marks, and realised the cost had been forgotten while counting money.

qa.q: What could Pankaj do next term, and why?
qa.a: Pankaj could limit the batches to what the timetable allows and keep evenings before tests free, because the marks are the reason for studying.

qa.q: How might Shankar see Pankaj's answer that the money was worth it?
qa.a: Shankar was probably worried and unsure how to help, since a friend who is tired and missing lectures says everything is fine.

grounding: A student takes five tutoring batches, attendance and sleep suffer and marks fall, so the extra income has a real cost.

passage:
Advisor's note, 14 March. Irfan, class advisor, B.Com second year.
Ishita's attendance has dropped from ninety percent in August to sixty-one percent now. Today I asked her to stay back after class. She told me she runs five tuition batches for school children: one at six in the morning before college, and four between five and nine at night. 'The money helps at home,' she said, and I believe her.
She fell asleep twice in my accounts lecture last week. Her mid-term score was 38 out of 100; last year she topped the class in the same paper. She kept rubbing her eyes while we talked. 'I thought I could manage all of it.'
I didn't tell her to stop earning. We looked at which batches take the most hours. I have also referred her to the college counsellor and will follow up next Monday.

qa.q: How can you tell that Ishita feels worn out and let down by herself?
qa.a: She falls asleep in lectures, keeps rubbing her eyes and says she thought she could manage it all, which sounds exhausted and disappointed.

qa.q: What else could Ishita try so earning doesn't cost her studies?
qa.a: She could keep only one or two batches and protect her sleep and class hours, with the counsellor helping her plan the change.

qa.q: How does the situation look to Irfan as her advisor?
qa.a: Irfan sees a strong student sliding and understands the family need, so the advisor helps her cut back instead of scolding her.

grounding: Shows a student taking on five tutoring batches until attendance, sleep and marks fall, so the income carries a real cost.

passage:
Thursday night, 1:10 a.m.
Darshan, write this down so you remember it. Got internals back. 11 out of 30 in circuits. Gurpreet got 24 and she didn't even study that much, she just came to class.
I came to class three times this month. Because of the batches. Five of them now. Two in the morning, three after college. The last one ends at 9:30 and I'm home by 10:15, eating cold rice. Then assignments. Sleeping maybe five hours.
I took the fifth batch because the parents asked nicely and it was ₹2,500 more a month. I felt rich for about a week.
Today Sir asked if everything was all right at home. It is. It's me.
Tomorrow I'm telling the Class 9 parents I'll stop after this month. Need to sleep now. Actually sleep.

qa.q: What did Darshan score in circuits?
What does 'It is. It's me.' suggest about how Darshan feels?
qa.a: Darshan feels ashamed and tired, blaming the choice to take on too much rather than anything at home.

qa.q: Which approach would suit Darshan better next term?
qa.a: Setting a firm limit on batches before term starts and keeping exam weeks free, so sleep and classes stay protected.

qa.q: How might the Class 9 parents feel when Darshan steps back?
qa.a: They may be disappointed to lose a tutor their child knows, but a month's notice gives them time to find someone else.

grounding: Shows a student taking a fifth tutoring batch until attendance, sleep and marks fall, and deciding to drop one.
